body_en_plain:
January, 1993     Page Reply


 How to write to us...02     -
 G.C. Wells...........03    05
 Peter Wheeler........06    08
 Phil Parnell.........09    17
 Andrew Fleming.......20    22
 George Munro.........28    29
 Kevin Snowdon........32    39
 M.R. Bennett.........44    45

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: G.C. Wells, THETFORD

Dear Ron and Brian,

Yes, the old Gitt is back, and
as you know from the past I am
not all that up to scratch,
(must have caught something from
the dog, scratch scratch).


Here we go again. How can I get
a print of the clip art [in
ANIMAL FORM - OUTLET 35] without
the numbers and is it possible
for other full-size clips, such
as Frogclip No.51, to be printed
smaller and is it possible to
separate various pictures when
you have more than one printing
together as in Church clip.


Now, I know I am in for a
blaggin' from you pair for my
ignorance and lack of computer
know how, but there you go. Can
you get 5 airgun pellets in a 1
inch circle at 35 yards? If the
answer is no then at least I
have the edge on you, at that.
Well! anyway, not to worry.

        Yours as ever,

          G.C. Wells
        (The old Gitt)

Brian Cavers to George Wells

No, but I might manage 1 airgun
pellet in a 35-yard circle from
5 inches. Will that do?

To print parts of those pictures
just save them as SCREENS using
SAVE...etc. "name" SCREEN$ (or
in the monthly clip art just use
the built-in SAVE option) and
then load the SCREEN$ into CLIP
COMPOSER (OUTLET 29) which will
let you alter areas of pictures.
I can't remember off-hand if an
"erase area" option is included
but you can certainly "grab" a
blank bit of the screen and drop
it on top of a part you do not
want in order to wipe it!
                        - Brian

From: P.Wheeler, WARLINGHAM

Dear Brian and Ron,

Although I tend to use Jacksoft
more, I have used DRKODE without
trouble until recently when I
tried to assemble ADD A,D and
got the 'syntax?' report. I then
discovered that ADC and SBC also
failed i.e all which used the
code combination LD DE,nn :CALL
61901: LD A,n: JP 62416 in the
programs code. My source code
appeared to be correctly entered
at 25000 and above, e.g. ADD was
129. EX AF,AF' which uses LD
DE,nn & CALL 61901 also SUB
which uses LD A,n and JP 62416
are both accepted. In fact I
can't find anything that looks
wrong, so Hel---p!

At the time of Issue 39 I was
putting 3 OUTLETs on 1 disc so I
haven't kept the original but
both my backup copies do the
same thing. I've included a copy
of my faulty DRKODE with this
letter and would be grateful for
a clean copy.

Wishing you both a Happy Xmas
and a Prosperous (literally) New
Year.

         Peter Wheeler

Brian Cavers to Peter Wheeler

In some machine code assemblers,
opcodes without a named register
default to the accumulator:i.e.,
the A register. Dr. Kode is such
an assembler so for the opcode:
"ADD A,D" just enter:"ADD D" and
the same for ADC, SBC etc. This
is because these 8-bit additions
and subtractions can ONLY be
done using the A register. I do
not personally like the method
as it scarcely saves much time
and is just confusing but you do
get used to it!

                        - Brian

From: Mr.P. Parnell,

Firstly, here is a bit of an
apology and also some info. I
wrote to you a while ago about
triple line spacing from the
modified printer routine in
BLAST IT. It wasn't my set-up
that was at fault, well not
fully, as the textfile I LOADed
up was spaced like that! Have
you ever felt a fool or what?!
An extra linefeed was supplied
by yours truly, Mr +3.

It seems that both the Amstrad
DMP3000 and DMP4000 series use
pin 14 to force AUTO-LF, so this
line must be cut,or prised away,
on the connection to the printer
cable.

NB this pin is referred to as
AFD rather than AUTO-FEED XT in
the manual). Then you will be
able to set the dipswitch on the
printer to either CR or CR-LF as
you wish. If you don't do this
then the dipswitch will always
be overidden by the +3 and no
matter which way you have the
dipswitch set you'll always get
double line feed on a carriage
return.

These printers do not have an
escape sequence for setting or
clearing AUTO-LF.Amstrad strikes
again! This is why I have been
having all these problems with
my printer. Just goes to show
that you're never to old to
learn, eh?

Recently, I went to the Alter-
native Micro Show in Stafford- I
go every year(NOT to be confused
with the All Formats Fair).There
are actually lots of bargains
for the Speccy at AMS and NONE
at All Format shows. I came away
with armfuls of stuff for very
little hard earned dosh!


It is only `2 entry (1.50 if you
order an advanced ticket) and is
nearly always on in the first
couple of weeks in November.
Sadly, it is a one day a year
event and by the time you read
this you will have missed it.
OUTLET should go there as it is
always packed solid, and I do
mean solid!


There were even stalls for the
Electron and other bygone comp-
uters. There was one stall that
had racks upon racks of micro-
drive carts at 50p each! I
thought they were difficult to
get hold of?!

The other day I was messing
about with the quad density
option of my printer. This is a
far better quality print out and
I was wondering if you had a
quad density program in your
collection? I could really do
with one that allows you to vary
the size and position of the
dump. Has anyone out there got
one or will it remain as a
fantasy of mine for the rest of
my days?


Moving on to the subscription. I
for one would not mind paying
that bit extra for my OUTLET if
it ensured that I could continue
to receive quality programs such
as yours.


I have noticed on looking back
on my old issues that from about
Issue 50 odd the content has
been steadily but surely
decreasing. At one time it was
common to have a loading menu
that went from A to W,X or even
Z but now it never seems to get
past P or Q. I wish I could help
on this score but I am only a
novice. So come on all you
people with talent out there.
Get them fingers tapping!


I would like to ask about sub-
scription while I am at it. The
last issue (No.63) was the last
one of my 12 month subs. Should
I leave the standing order as it
is and wait for you to send me a
new order for my bank to process
This is what the editorial seems
to say.

How is the new legislation on
cheques affecting you? I know
that FORMAT absolutely refuses
to accept any of the new
cheques. I cannot see the reason
for his stubborn attitude my-
self. If he had been on the re-
ceiving end of fraudulent cheque
encashment, as so many people
seem to have been of late, then
I feel sure that he would be
singing a different tune!!

The law was so heavily on the
side of the banks,ANY change can
only be for the better.

The annoying part about it is I
have had to order a special
cheque book printed just to
please him that does not have
the words "a/c payee" on them.
If one is stolen and cashed on
the way to him then my money has
gone for a burton and there is
absolutely nothing I can do
about it! As it stands now the
bank would have to reimburse me
if they cashed it into any other
account than the payee's. Much
better.Especially as since after
the new year ANY alteration of
the cheque will render it
invalid.

By the way, thanks very much for
the TASWORD +3 screen fonts in
OUTLET Issue 61 - they worked a
treat. Much better than all that
nasty typing! I wrote to Tasman
and told them that you said that
he was an idiot - only kidding,
but he was, wasn't he?!

Anyway, I have said enough for
two I think and so I will sign
off now. A special thanks to all
those that got in touch to buy
my software and to you for
helping me sell it.

              Phil

Brian Cavers to Phil Parnell

A quad-density dump is planned
for next month's OUTLET although
note that quad-density cannot
simply print a same-size screen
dump in higher quality. It just
prints the dots closer together
so the final image is smaller!

To print a giant image in high
resolution you would need to
somehow print several screens
side by side. Some large text
routines also use quad density;
each letter is printed one by
one using the quad graphics mode
and so the entire width of the
printer line can be filled.

Nevertheless you can experiment!

Each month,the main OUTLET fills
almost exactly the same space of
about 180K to fit the Opus disc
(and the former two microdrive
cartridges). This has been true
within a few K since we launched
in 1987. However, some months,
if there are more large programs
then naturally the total number
of items shown on the CONTENTS
page will be less. This is true
this month where we have TETRIS,
CANDIDATE and PLANETS all over
20K each. Another month there
might be a lot of small programs
and in theory the CONTENTS page
could be crammed up to X,Y, Z
but the space filled on the disc
would still be the same.

ADD-ENDERS is added to the above
of course.

The new legislation on cheques
will only affect anyone who
sends in a crossed cheque made
out to the wrong name. Cheques
should be made out to CHEZRON
SOFTWARE. It doesn't matter if
your cheque is crossed or not so
long as the name is correct.

                        - Brian

From: Andrew Fleming, DEVIZES

Dear Brian and Ron,

HELP! PLEASE, from anybody. A
few months ago I got 'UNIdos'
and carefully went through the
instructions to install it in my
Plus D then reconfigured some of
my OUTLET discs. I got so many
'sector errors' I very quickly
reverted to 'Betados'.

I've had some success in getting
rid of some of the sector errors
using the byte editing facilit-
ies of GLENSOFT PROFILE. What I
need is a real 'idiots' guide to
the contents of directory tracks
and sectors. How to obtain/calc-
ulate the values needed on 1+1=2
basis.

Maybe you can persuade one of
the wizards of the Plus D to do
a comprehensive article on this
aspect of computing?

        Yours sincerely,

         Andrew Fleming

Brian Cavers to Andrew Fleming

I don't have UNIDOS so I cannot
help there I'm afraid. Can't you
go back to your supplier? Surely
they must help? Anyone else?

Regarding your existing corrupt
discs,you might also try our own
SEEK 'N PEEK in OUTLET 45. On
the next page are details of the
40 directory sectors on Tracks 0
to 3. Each sector holds two file
details, the second one offset
by 256 bytes from the start of
the sector. The first byte, the
filetype, is 1 for a BASIC file
and... 2=Numeric Array, 3=String
Array, 4=Code, 5=48K Snapshot,
6=m/drive, 7=SCREEN$, 8=Special,
9=128K snapshot, 10=Opentype,
11=Execute. 0 means erased.

 Byte No.         Remarks
 --------         -------
  1       : Filetype
  2 -  11 : Filename
 12 -  13 : No.of sectors(hi-lo)
 14 -  15 : 1st track/sector
 16 - 210 : Bit Map
211       : pages length (128K?)
212       : Filetype(not erased)
213 - 214 : File length
215 - 216 : 1st address of code
217 - 218 : Vars start (BASIC?)
219 - 220 : Auto start

I don't think 221 to 256 are in
use by the standard dos but may
be by UNIDOS or BETADOS. Note
that bytes 215 to 216 will be
23755 if the file is BASIC. All
double-byte values are the usual
low-high byte order except bytes
12 to 13 which are high-low.

Remember to add 256 to the byte
number if you are looking at the
SECOND file in each 512 byte
sector.

The sectors used by each file
are represented by one set bit
in the bit map. This is tricky
to examine in BASIC and to
explain. If you want to explore
it then I suggest you format a
blank disc and save one file
(which will then start at Track
4, sector 1) and compare the
binary positions in the map. In
use, the system "merges" the bit
map from each directory entry to
form an overall bit map of the
whole disc so it can see which
sectors are free rapidly (if you
know machine code then they are
'OR'd together).

The bit map is not used by the
system to load files. Instead,
the FIRST track and sector of
the file is extracted from byte
14 to 15 of the directory entry;
this is loaded and the LAST TWO
BYTES OF THE FILE SECTOR HAS THE
TRACK AND SECTOR OF THE NEXT
SECTOR OF THE FILE TO BE LOADED.
The very last sector of a file
has these last two bytes set at
0. So, this is how you might try
to reconstruct a file. You might
copy these sectors one by one to
a new disc and create part of a
directory entry (without the bit
map). I think you could then
copy it in the normal way to a
new disc. The dos would then
create a proper directory entry
complete with bit map.

However, having said all that,
the very fact that you are gett-
ing errors suggest that part of
the above information is corrupt
or missing so the system cannot
find all the data. It may not be
possible for you to do any
better. Even if you reconstruct
a file there may be corruption
within the file itself. This is
why I rarely try file recovery.
It can be extremely difficult
and very time-consuming (much
like hacking).

One other thing,the FIRST sector
of each file (not the directory
entry but the actual first sect-
or used by the file itself) has
a short header at the start.This
is as follows...

 Byte No.       Remarks
 --------       -------
  1      : Filetype
  2 - 3  : File length
  4 - 5  : Start address
  6 - 9  : Don't know!

I don't know what the last few
bytes are but I am pretty sure
the whole header is 9 bytes long
and the actual file starts at
byte 10. Remember, this is only
only on the file's first sector.
So, a file will have 512 bytes
in its first sector LESS the 9
bytes of the header LESS the 2
bytes at the end = 501 bytes.All
its subsequent sectors will have
510 bytes of file data plus just
the two bytes at the end. Hope
that helps!
                      - Brian

From: George Munro, LONDON

There are two things I urgently
require:

a) 'FAILSAFE' FOR THE +D

B)  PEEK possibility to put into
    a program so that the
    program can call up the
    actual drive in force.
    e.g. like the PEEK 23766
    for the microdrive.

Once I have these I think I can
let you have a good program to
make headings and things for
videos etc.

           Yours Aye,

                  - George Munro


Brian Cavers to George Munro

We have no +D equivalent to the
microdrive FAILSAFE I'm afraid,
George.However,you might be able
to achieve what you want using
the Disciple/+D error disable
poke. If you POKE 23728,1 then
any errors are ignored. However,
it will not automatically jump
to a special line so you need
some method of detecting any
fault.

For example,if,say, your program
loads code to address 55555 then
you might POKE 55555,99: POKE
55556,99: POKE 55557,99 before
loading(or any values that would
be impossible or unlikely to be
in the loaded code). You then
test after loading thus...

1000 POKE 55555,99
1010 POKE 23728,1
1020 LOAD N$ CODE 55555
1030 POKE 23728,0
1040 IF PEEK 55555=99 THEN GOTO

Note the POKE 23728,0 at line
1030 which switches OFF the
error disable.

If you are loading say a string
array called X$ then you might
use say,DIM X$(1) before loading
and then use IF LEN X$(1)=1 THEN
GOTO.

When experimenting, take care to
save your program first and make
sure you have a 23728,0 as you
may find you cannot break in at
all!

To LOAD, SAVE, CAT etc. the
"current" drive you need only
use an asterisk instead of the
drive number,e.g., LOAD d*;"XX".

Remember, however, any program
that uses features exclusive to
the Disciple/+D will not work
unaltered on other systems and
if too time-consuming or imposs-
ible for us to change then it
might only appear in ADD-ENDERS
on the Disciple/+D version only.

It helps if you include a list
of machine-specific lines in a
program else we have to search
every line. It's better to use
our standard load system that
works on any system (see lines
9500-9599 and 9600-9699 in most
programs that load data. -Brian.

From: K. Snowdon, TYNE & WEAR

Dear Ron and Brian,

I wonder if you could help with
a problem I have with my +D and
3.5 DD disk drive. Every time I
try to boot up the Systems disk
the drive starts up and runs for
a while then I get the error
code:

 0:1 SECTOR ERROR O:1

This happens with all the disks
I have with the Systems file on.
I have tried LOADing the System
from the +D tape but the same
error is generated no matter
which command I enter (SAVE,
LOAD, CAT or FORMAT).


I have tried cleaning the edge
connector and I also tested
every track of the ribbon cable,
which seemed OK.

This leads me to the conclusion
that either the disk drive is
faulty or the +D interface. Have
you come across this problem
before? If you think the +D is
at fault is there anywhere that
repairs them or perhaps it would
be cheaper to buy a second hand
one.  Alternatively, do you know
of anyone who would try my +D on
their set? I would, of course,
pay for the postage etc.

[I sent Kevin my copy of the dos
in case his was corrupt and then
suggested he also check his set
up. His reply follows...   -BC]

Thank you for taking the trouble
to answer my letter regarding my
+D and 3.5 DD/DS disk drive.
Unfortunately, the DOS disk you
sent gave the same result as
mine i.e. SECTOR ERROR when
trying to Boot The SYS disk.

As you mentioned in your letter,
the drive could be at fault. I
purchased a 3.5" 1-meg drive at
an All Formats Fair for `25.00.
It was a Citizen Drive almost
identical to the one I was using
with my +D.

I put the bare drive into the
Drive housing, connected it up
to the power supply and the +D
interface then turned it on:
nothing.

I remembered reading in an
earlier OUTLET that some drives
have a switch to select the
drive number, and on closer in-
spection I found a small switch
beside the power connection on
the back of the drive. Then, by
trial and error, I got the drive
running and working with the +D.

Prior to me getting the drive
fault I was getting more and
more sector errors and could
only format a disk up to sector
760. Now, with hindsight, the
drive was very much on the way
out.

There is one strange thing about
this new drive, the LED is on
all the time even though the
drive is not running.

Is this usual for new drives?
The LED goes out if I press the
reset on the side of my Spectrum
128K.

With the drive working, I was at
last able to read December's
OUTLET and was very saddened to
read that the SAM vesion might
be discontinued. I thought the
numbers of SAM owners was on par
with the numbers of +D/Disciple
readers, so it is worrying to
think that with this large
readership disappearing it might
affect the future of OUTLET, I
hope not.

Looking to the future, is Brian
Gaff going to send in a review
of the Spectrum Emulater for the
PC?

I would be very interested to
find out more about it.


Have you any plans to try a PC
Disk based magazine? From what I
have read there are very few for
the machine and with the PC
being so user-unfriendly I am
sure a PC Disk magazine of the
quality of OUTLET would have a
readership. I know this would be
like starting again but I think
we all realise that the Spectrum
will disappear eventually and it
would be a great shame for the
CHEZRON team to go with it. You
could also use Brian Gaff's
emulator as a sort of trans-
itional vehicle to go over to
the PC.


Once again, thank you for your
help and here's wishing you a
Happy Christmas and a prosperous
New Year.

         Kevin Snowdon

Brian Cavers to Kevin Snowdon

Yes, it definitely sounds like a
drive fault. When you say you
could only format a disc up to
760 sectors, I assume you mean
up to Track 75? That is, there
are 80 tracks on each side of a
disc, numbered 0 to 79 on side 1
and 128 to 207 on side 2. Each
track has 10 sectors. If you
could only format up to Track 79
it might suggest your drive is
either only a single-sided drive
or there is a switch which is
set for single-sided. I would
only expect this to cause errors
on discs which are more than
half-full. Drives vary as to
whether the LED remains lit. If
you use two drives they show
which is the "current" drive.

You should also check that other
settings are correct. The track
setting should be 208. This can
be set in the setup program but
you can also just POKE @1,208
for drive 1 and POKE @2,208 for
drive 2 and resave the dos if it
is O.K.

A more likely candidate for the
errors might be the step rate.It
is 6 by default but your drive
may work better at a slower rate
so try POKE @3,12 or POKE @3,15.


This POKE affects both drives if
you should have two. Once again,
if successful,resave the dos for
a permanent fix.

The +D version of OUTLET is not
so vulnerable as the SAM because

(a) we are getting loads of
Spectrum contributions and...

(b)it can always be run as a
hobby even if I get full-time
employment so long as there are
at least a reasonable number
that are still interested, say,
one hundred. This is doubly true
because Chris Oliver is editing
the main program section while I
am doing the text. The Opus and
tape versions and even the +3
versions are vulnerable though
because of the time needed to
convert to those systems and the
Opus and tape versions do not
sell many at all now.

If Brian Gaff is reading this he
might well send in a review of
the emulator but bear in mind
that he is selling it. It would
be more appropriate if someone
else did a review. I cannot
because I don't have a PC!

As for us producing a PC version
of OUTLET, we have certainly
pondered the idea but there are
many difficulties...

1.Some things taken for granted
on the Spectrum are difficult on
a PC! It may not be possible to
produce a "linked" magazine in
quite the way we do now.

2. We don't know enough to give
out techical advice (not crucial
but it helps!)

3. As usual, we have no cash to
finance such a venture.

4. Having worked ourselves into
the ground for five years with
little general recognition and
no financial reward (CHEZRON has
generated only a bare survival
salary for one person plus a
meagre part-time wage for one
other yet has been run by three
people doing the equivalent of
four to five people's full-time
work! Needless to say, morale is
so low that we would want a more
substantial start than just the
wild enthusiasm with which we
started the Spectrum OUTLET!

5.Although the PC market is huge
it also has MASSIVE competition
from PD/Shareware!      - BRIAN

From: M.R. Bennett, BUCKINGHAM



How about a print routine for a
3.5" disc label in a future
issue?

         M.R. Bennett

Brian Cavers to M.R. Bennett

I've given this some thought and
think quite a good disc labeller
program could be produced using
PFN PRINT (OUTLET 59) to create
a text screen printed out using
the Z3 option in SCOPY (should
be next month). The program will
need to cope with both 3" and
3.5" discs (fortunately the same
width label!) and a machine code
routine to turn the screen
upside down is also needed as
the 3" side B must be upside
down and also, some people like
the 3.5" side A upside down too.
Two text screens would need to
be created and stored in memory
for disc sides A and B (although
some do not use the 3.5" side B
of the label).

Sticky labels are available on
greaseproof, tractor-fed paper
but I think most would prefer to
have the labels printed on norm-
al paper with a box drawn round
to guide in cutting out and then
any suitable glue used to stick
the label to the disc. PRITT is
best for this sort of job as it
is similar to the sort of glue
that is on sellotape - it sticks
instantly and will not run into
any cracks in the disc!

A decent text editor would be
needed to enable input, display
and modification of the text on
the screen.I see it storing each
line of text in an array with
details of height so any line
could be deleted and reprinted.

I'll see if I can find time to
look at this unless anyone else
would like to volunteer?!!

                        - Brian.

## Letters (1)

January, 1993     Page Reply

How to write to us...02     - G.C. Wells...........03    05 Peter Wheeler........06    08 Phil Parnell.........09    17 Andrew Fleming.......20    22 George Munro.........28    29 Kevin Snowdon........32    39 M.R. Bennett.........44    45

PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE! Text is accepted in any form for OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files (say which),typed or handwritten letters. However, PLEASE send us a textfile if possible so your letter needn't be typed again! The easiest for us to edit are Tasword 2 files with the right margin set at 32 but a textfile in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be parts of your letter you do not wish published but we always use our discretion anyway. Letters may also be edited for clarity and length... Please ask if you welcome direct correspondence from other OUTLET readers and we will publish your full address.

From: G.C. Wells, THETFORD

Dear Ron and Brian,

Yes, the old Gitt is back, and as you know from the past I am not all that up to scratch, (must have caught something from the dog, scratch scratch).

Here we go again. How can I get a print of the clip art [in ANIMAL FORM - OUTLET 35] without the numbers and is it possible for other full-size clips, such as Frogclip No.51, to be printed smaller and is it possible to separate various pictures when you have more than one printing together as in Church clip.

Now, I know I am in for a blaggin' from you pair for my ignorance and lack of computer know how, but there you go. Can you get 5 airgun pellets in a 1 inch circle at 35 yards? If the answer is no then at least I have the edge on you, at that. Well! anyway, not to worry.

Yours as ever,

G.C. Wells (The old Gitt)

Regarding your existing corrupt discs,you might also try our own SEEK 'N PEEK in OUTLET 45. On the next page are details of the 40 directory sectors on Tracks 0 to 3. Each sector holds two file details, the second one offset by 256 bytes from the start of the sector. The first byte, the filetype, is 1 for a BASIC file and... 2=Numeric Array, 3=String Array, 4=Code, 5=48K Snapshot, 6=m/drive, 7=SCREEN$, 8=Special, 9=128K snapshot, 10=Opentype, 11=Execute. 0 means erased.

Byte No.         Remarks

```text
 --------         -------
```

1       : Filetype 2 -  11 : Filename 12 -  13 : No.of sectors(hi-lo) 14 -  15 : 1st track/sector 16 - 210 : Bit Map 211       : pages length (128K?) 212       : Filetype(not erased) 213 - 214 : File length 215 - 216 : 1st address of code 217 - 218 : Vars start (BASIC?) 219 - 220 : Auto start

I don't think 221 to 256 are in use by the standard dos but may be by UNIDOS or BETADOS. Note that bytes 215 to 216 will be 23755 if the file is BASIC. All double-byte values are the usual low-high byte order except bytes 12 to 13 which are high-low.

Remember to add 256 to the byte number if you are looking at the SECOND file in each 512 byte sector.

The sectors used by each file are represented by one set bit in the bit map. This is tricky to examine in BASIC and to explain. If you want to explore it then I suggest you format a blank disc and save one file (which will then start at Track 4, sector 1) and compare the binary positions in the map. In use, the system "merges" the bit map from each directory entry to form an overall bit map of the whole disc so it can see which sectors are free rapidly (if you know machine code then they are 'OR'd together).

The bit map is not used by the system to load files. Instead, the FIRST track and sector of the file is extracted from byte 14 to 15 of the directory entry; this is loaded and the LAST TWO BYTES OF THE FILE SECTOR HAS THE TRACK AND SECTOR OF THE NEXT SECTOR OF THE FILE TO BE LOADED. The very last sector of a file has these last two bytes set at 0. So, this is how you might try to reconstruct a file. You might copy these sectors one by one to a new disc and create part of a directory entry (without the bit map). I think you could then copy it in the normal way to a new disc. The dos would then create a proper directory entry complete with bit map.

However, having said all that, the very fact that you are gett- ing errors suggest that part of the above information is corrupt or missing so the system cannot find all the data. It may not be possible for you to do any better. Even if you reconstruct a file there may be corruption within the file itself. This is why I rarely try file recovery. It can be extremely difficult and very time-consuming (much like hacking).

One other thing,the FIRST sector of each file (not the directory entry but the actual first sect- or used by the file itself) has a short header at the start.This is as follows...

Byte No.       Remarks

```text
 --------       -------
```

1      : Filetype 2 - 3  : File length 4 - 5  : Start address 6 - 9  : Don't know!

I don't know what the last few bytes are but I am pretty sure the whole header is 9 bytes long and the actual file starts at byte 10. Remember, this is only only on the file's first sector. So, a file will have 512 bytes in its first sector LESS the 9 bytes of the header LESS the 2 bytes at the end = 501 bytes.All its subsequent sectors will have 510 bytes of file data plus just the two bytes at the end. Hope that helps! - Brian

Каждый сектор содержит данные о двух файлах, причем запись второго сдвинута на 256 байт от начала сектора. Первый байт — тип файла: 1 для BASIC-файла, 2 = числовой массив, 3 = строковый массив, 4 = Code, 5 = 48K Snapshot, 6 = m/drive, 7 = SCREEN$, 8 = Special, 9 = 128K snapshot, 10 = Opentype, 11 = Execute. 0 означает удаленный файл.

```text
 Номер байта     Описание
 -----------     --------
  1            : Тип файла
  2 -  11      : Имя файла
 12 -  13      : Кол-во секторов (старший-младший)
 14 -  15      : Начальные дорожка/сектор
 16 - 210      : Битовая карта (Bit Map)
211            : Длина в страницах (128K?)
212            : Тип файла (не удален)
213 - 214      : Длина файла
215 - 216      : Начальный адрес кодового блока
217 - 218      : Начало переменных (BASIC?)
219 - 220      : Автостарт
```

Не думаю, что байты с 221 по 256 используются стандартной DOS, но они могут применяться в UNIDOS или BETADOS. Обратите внимание, что байты с 215 по 216 будут равны 23755, если файл является программой на BASIC. Все двухбайтовые значения идут в обычном порядке «младший-старший» (low-high), за исключением байтов 12 и 13, где порядок обратный — «старший-младший» (high-low).

Не забывайте прибавлять 256 к номеру байта, если вы просматриваете ВТОРОЙ файл в 512-байтном секторе.

Секторы, занятые каждым файлом, представлены установленными битами в битовой карте. Анализировать это в BASIC и объяснять довольно сложно. Если хотите поэкспериментировать, предлагаю отформатировать чистый диск, сохранить один файл (он начнется с дорожки 4, сектор 1) и сопоставить двоичные позиции в карте. В процессе работы система объединяет битовые карты из каждого элемента каталога для формирования общей битовой карты всего диска, чтобы быстро определять свободные секторы (если вы знакомы с машинным кодом — они объединяются по логическому «OR»).

Битовая карта не используется системой для загрузки файлов. Вместо этого ПЕРВЫЕ дорожка и сектор файла берутся из байтов 14 и 15 записи в каталоге; этот сектор загружается, а ПОСЛЕДНИЕ ДВА БАЙТА СЕКТОРА ФАЙЛА СОДЕРЖАТ НОМЕРА ДОРОЖКИ И СЕКТОРА СЛЕДУЮЩЕГО СЕКТОРА ФАЙЛА, КОТОРЫЙ НУЖНО ЗАГРУЗИТЬ. В самом последнем секторе файла эти два байта равны 0. Таким образом, именно так можно попытаться восстановить файл: вы можете сектор за сектором скопировать эти данные на новый диск и вручную воссоздать часть записи в каталоге (без битовой карты). ```

### Brian Cavers отвечает George Munro

Боюсь, George, у нас нет точного аналога утилиты FAILSAFE для +D. Однако вы можете добиться желаемого, используя отключение ошибок в Disciple/+D через POKE. Если сделать `POKE 23728,1`, любые ошибки дисковода будут игнорироваться. Правда, автоматического перехода на заданную строку не произойдет, поэтому вам понадобится способ проверки сбоя.

Например, если ваша программа загружает кодовый блок по адресу 55555, перед загрузкой можно выполнить `POKE 55555,99: POKE 55556,99: POKE 55557,99` (или записать любые другие значения, появление которых в загружаемом коде невозможно или маловероятно). После загрузки вы делаете проверку:

```text
1000 POKE 55555,99
1010 POKE 23728,1
1020 LOAD N$ CODE 55555
1030 POKE 23728,0
1040 IF PEEK 55555=99 THEN GOTO ...
```

Обратите внимание на `POKE 23728,0` в строке 1030 — это возвращает стандартную обработку ошибок.

Если вы загружаете, к примеру, строковый массив с именем X$, перед загрузкой можно объявить `DIM X$(1)`, а затем проверить: `IF LEN X$(1)=1 THEN GOTO ...`

Во время экспериментов не забывайте заранее сохранять программу и всегда следите за возвратом `23728,0`, иначе при ошибке вы вообще не сможете прервать выполнение по BREAK!

Чтобы выполнять LOAD, SAVE, CAT и т. д. для «текущего» дисковода, достаточно использовать звездочку вместо номера привода, например: `LOAD d*;"XX"`.

Помните, однако: любая программа, использующая уникальные возможности Disciple/+D, не будет работать без изменений на других системах. И если адаптация потребует слишком много времени или окажется невозможной, программа выйдет только в рубрике ADD-ENDERS и исключительно в версии для Disciple/+D.

Очень помогает, если авторы присылают список специфичных для конкретного «железа» строк программы, иначе нам приходится прочесывать весь листинг. Лучше использовать нашу стандартную подпрограмму загрузки, которая работает везде (см. строки 9500–9599 и 9600–9699 в большинстве программ журнала, загружающих данные).

### Brian Cavers отвечает Kevin Snowdon

Да, это определенно была поломка дисковода. Когда вы пишете, что диск форматировался только до 760 секторов, полагаю, вы имеете в виду до 75-й дорожки? На каждой стороне диска по 80 дорожек: с 0 по 79 на стороне 1 и со 128 по 207 на стороне 2. На каждой дорожке по 10 секторов. Если форматирование останавливалось на 79-й дорожке, это наводит на мысль, что ваш дисковод либо односторонний, либо переключатель был выставлен в односторонний режим. Впрочем, проблемы это должно было вызывать только при заполнении диска более чем наполовину. Поведение светодиода у разных моделей различается: у некоторых он горит постоянно. При использовании двух дисководов индикатор показывает, какой из них активен в данный момент.

Вам также стоит проверить остальные настройки. Количество дорожек должно быть установлено на 208. Это можно задать в программе настройки, но можно и просто выполнить `POKE @1,208` для дисковода 1 и `POKE @2,208` для дисковода 2, после чего пересохранить DOS, если все работает нормально.

Более вероятной причиной ошибок могла быть скорость шага (step rate). По умолчанию она равна 6, но ваш дисковод может надежнее работать на более низкой скорости, так что попробуйте `POKE @3,12` или `POKE @3,15`.

Этот POKE влияет на оба дисковода, если у вас их два. Опять же, если помогло — сохраните DOS заново для постоянного применения настроек.

Brian Cavers отвечает M.R. Bennett:

Я поразмыслил над этим и полагаю, что вполне приличную программу для печати этикеток можно сделать на базе PFN PRINT (OUTLET 59) — формировать текстовый экран и распечатывать его с помощью опции Z3 в SCOPY (должна появиться в следующем месяце). Программа должна поддерживать как 3", так и 3.5" диски (к счастью, ширина наклеек у них одинаковая!). Кроме того, понадобится подпрограмма в машинных кодах для переворачивания экрана вверх ногами, поскольку на 3" дисках сторона B должна быть перевёрнута, да и на 3.5" диске некоторым нравится, чтобы сторона A тоже была вверх ногами. Потребуется создавать и хранить в памяти два текстовых экрана — для сторон A и B (хотя некоторые и не используют сторону B на 3.5" наклейках).

Самоклеящиеся этикетки продаются на вощёной бумаге для тракторной подачи, но, думаю, большинству удобнее печатать наклейки на обычной бумаге с рамкой-контуром для вырезания, а затем приклеивать любым подходящим клеем. Для этих целей лучше всего подходит PRITT, так как он похож на клейкий слой скотча — схватывается мгновенно и не затечёт в щели на корпусе дискеты!

Потребуется приличный текстовый редактор для ввода, отображения и редактирования текста на экране. Мне это видится так: каждая строка текста хранится в массиве с параметрами высоты, чтобы любую строку можно было удалить и перепечатать.

Постараюсь выкроить время и заняться этим, если только кто-нибудь другой не захочет вызваться добровольцем?!!

— Brian.
